impact_scope.description: The existing public restart_frame! lifecycle method now also clears the decoder's internal bitstream_is_closed state. Its signature, caller-supplied arguments, and call-order preconditions are unchanged.

evidence: S0 already declares decoder.restart_frame!(index, io_position) as a public callable lifecycle path.
H0 initializes the JPEG decoder and drives it through fuzz_image_decoder, but never calls restart_frame! or supplies its index and io_position arguments.
S1 retains the same public decoder.restart_frame!(index, io_position) declaration and adds only an internal bitstream_is_closed reset.
Unchanged H0 still never calls restart_frame!; no new argument, configuration, entry point, or call-order action is required to reach that same callable surface.

new_harness_obligation.description: The added state reset is internal to the already-existing, already-omitted restart_frame! call. The separate closed-bitstream behavior is reached through H0's existing decode path and does not require H0 to supply a new internal argument or configuration.
evidence: restart_frame!'s signature and caller-visible preconditions are identical in S0 and S1.
H0 already calls decode_frame through the image-decoder interface; source closure and bitstream_is_closed handling occur internally.

reason: For the anchored existing restart_frame! lifecycle unit, the exposure gap is true on both sides. S1 adds internal state-reset behavior but no concrete new H0 action and no reduction in same-scope reachability or control, so the fixed truth table yields UNCHANGED and no maintenance need.
